result:
The proposed answer, t, is wrong. The solution cites no actual result and gives no derivation.

A simple check is the case s = 1. Then C is an ordinary Reed–Solomon code of dimension t and length r. Its Schur square is the Reed–Solomon code of polynomials of degree at most 2t−2. The condition t ≤ (r+2s−1)/2 becomes 2t−1 ≤ r, so these polynomials evaluate injectively at the r points. The square therefore has dimension 2t−1, which is not t for any t ≥ 2. The conditions p ≥ t ≥ 2s are satisfied (for example s = 1, t = 2).

The general case shows the same thing. Codewords are the tuples (f^{(j)}(α_i)) for j < s. Their Schur products are spanned by tuples whose j-th component is C(a,j)C(b,j)·x^{a+b−2j}. These span a space far larger than t-dimensional, since already the j = 0 components give all of x^0, …, x^{2t−2}.

VERDICT: REJECT
